claims.claim_text: In February 2026 MicroVision closed the acquisition of substantially all of Luminar Technologies' worldwide lidar business (IRIS and HALO sensors) for a $33.0M purchase price funded with cash on hand, approved by the U.S. Bankruptcy Court on January 27, 2026.
claims.subject: MicroVision
claims.source_quote: On January 26, 2026, the Company entered into an agreement with Luminar Technologies, Inc. ... The acquisition was approved by the U.S. Bankruptcy Court on January 27, 2026. On February 3, 2026, the acquisition closed and MicroVision paid to Luminar the purchase price of $ 33.0 million (less the previously paid 10% deposit) plus cure costs of $ 0.2 million, funded through cash on hand.

claims.claim_text: MicroVision states it has over 700 issued and pending patents worldwide covering MEMS, LBS, laser diodes and related lidar systems.
claims.subject: MicroVision
claims.source_quote: Our extensive patent portfolio is large and broad, and we currently have over 700 issued patents and pending patents worldwide.

claims.claim_text: MicroVision states the automotive-grade IRIS sensor (1550nm time-of-flight long-range lidar acquired from Luminar) achieved start of production in April 2024.
claims.subject: IRIS sensor (acquired from Luminar)
claims.source_quote: The automotive-grade IRIS sensor achieved start of production in April 2024, with subsequent deliveries used in vehicles for road data collection and system training.

claims.claim_text: Glen W. DeVos, named MicroVision CEO in September 2025, previously served at Aptiv (and its predecessor Delphi Automotive) for 32 years, including as Senior Vice President from March 2017 to March 2024 and as Chief Technology Officer until January 2023.
claims.subject: Glen W. DeVos
claims.source_quote: Glen W. DeVos, age 64, was named Chief Executive Officer in September 2025 ... Prior to MicroVision, he served in various business leadership and technology roles at Aptiv and its predecessor Delphi Automotive from 1992 to March 2024. From March 2017 to March 2024, he was a Senior Vice President and he served as Chief Technology Officer until January 2023.

claims.claim_text: MicroVision recorded a series of 2025 impairment and write-down charges totaling roughly $25M (Ibeo perception software $10.1M; MOVIA L inventory $9.9M; MAVIN tooling $2.2M; MOVIA L adverse purchase commitment $3.2M) and in 2024 reduced its global workforce by approximately 41%, reflecting continued operating losses funded by ATM and convertible-note dilution.
claims.subject: MicroVision
claims.source_quote: In 2025, we recorded an impairment charge of $10.1 million in connection with perception software acquired from Ibeo, a $9.9 million write-down of select MOVIA L sensor inventory, as well as a $2.2 million impairment charge associated with certain production machinery and tooling equipment related to our MAVIN sensor. Additionally, in 2025, we recorded an adverse purchase commitment of $3.2 million related to the production of select MOVIA L sensor inventory. ... In 2024, to better align the Company s resources to support business needs, the Company reduced the global workforce by approximately 41 %.
